## Chef's Note

Add warm broth gradually and stir frequently, keeping the rice at a gentle simmer. Judge the finish by a tender center with a slight bite and a loose, creamy consistency. Return the cooked shrimp only at the end; lemon and basil brighten the rich rice.

## Directions

1.  **The Crunch:** In a large wide skillet, melt butter over medium-high. Add shrimp in a single layer. Cook on both sides until the flesh is pearly and opaque through the center, checking the thickest shrimp rather than relying on a fixed time. Work in batches if needed, sharing the butter between them. Remove to a clean plate; chop the large shrimp into bite-sized pieces if desired.
2.  **Foundation:** In the same pan, add onions and sauté for 2-3 minutes until translucent. Add garlic and sauté for 30-45 seconds.
3.  **Toast:** Add the Arborio rice. Stir for 2 minutes until the edges of the grains look translucent (The Toast Method).
4.  **Deglaze:** Pour in the wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
5.  **The Bind:** Reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Add hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring frequently and adding the next ladle when the previous one is mostly absorbed. Begin tasting after about 18–22 minutes; keep cooking and adding liquid until the center is tender with a slight bite. The full broth amount may not be needed; if it runs out before the rice is ready, continue with a little hot water.
6.  **The Texture:** Once the rice is al dente, stir in the heavy cream, Parmesan, lemon zest, and lemon juice to taste. Season with the listed salt and pepper. Loosen with a little hot broth or water if the rice sits in a stiff mound.
7.  **Combine:** Fold the seared shrimp and fresh basil into the risotto. Toss for 1 minute until the shrimp are warmed through.
8.  **Serve:** Garnish with optional extra basil and black pepper, and serve immediately. Allow about 50 minutes including preparation; extra shrimp batches or rice that needs longer will extend the time.

## Chef's Note

Add warm broth gradually and stir frequently, keeping the rice at a gentle simmer. Judge the finish by a tender center with a slight bite and a loose, creamy consistency. Return the cooked shrimp only at the end; lemon and basil brighten the rich rice. Serve as generous main-course portions.

## Directions

1. **Cook shrimp:** Use U10 shrimp (under 10 per pound) and unsalted butter for this stage. Melt all the butter over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp in a single layer, sharing the butter between batches if needed, until the thickest flesh is firm, pearly and opaque through the center. Transfer to a clean plate; chop into bite-sized pieces on a clean board if desired.
2. **Soften onion:** In the same pan add large onion; cook around 2–3 minutes until translucent, adjusting heat rather than letting the remaining butter burn.
3. **Add garlic:** Add garlic cloves and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
4. **Coat the rice:** Add Arborio rice and stir for about 2 minutes, until grain edges look translucent, without browning them darkly.
5. **Add wine:** Pour in dry white wine and stir until mostly absorbed.
6. **Hydrate gently:** Use chicken or vegetable broth and hot water for this stage. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring frequently and adding another when the previous is mostly absorbed. Begin tasting around 18–22 minutes; keep cooking until the center is tender with a slight bite. Use only as much broth as needed; if it runs out while rice remains firm, continue with a little hot water. Leave room for finishing additions.
7. **Finish the rice:** Use lemon, heavy cream, freshly grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper for this stage. Stir in the full heavy cream and Parmesan, all the lemon zest, and the lemon juice to taste. Use the listed salt and pepper allowances. Loosen stiff rice with a little remaining hot broth or water as needed; keep any unused lemon juice in a clean container separately rather than assuming every lemon produces the same amount.
8. **Return the shrimp:** Use fresh basil leaves for this stage. Fold in all the cooked shrimp and basil; warm briefly, starting around 1 minute and checking that the shrimp are warm throughout. Do not extend the rice simmer with shrimp already in it.
9. **Serve:** Use fresh basil (if using) for this stage. Use the optional extra basil, divide among the listed portions and serve immediately. Rice that needs more liquid/time or extra shrimp batches extends the approximate 50-minute schedule.

Cook the shrimp in a single layer, sharing the butter between batches if needed, until the thickest flesh is firm, pearly and opaque through the center. Transfer to a clean plate; chop into bite-sized pieces on a clean board if desired.
2. **Soften onion:** In the same pan add large onion; cook around 2–3 minutes until translucent, adjusting heat rather than letting the remaining butter burn.
3. **Add garlic:** Add garlic cloves and cook about 30–45 seconds until fragrant.
4. **Coat the rice:** Add Arborio rice and stir for about 2 minutes, until grain edges look translucent, without browning them darkly.
5. **Add wine:** Pour in dry white wine and stir until mostly absorbed.
6. **Hydrate gently:** Use chicken or vegetable broth and hot water for this stage. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Add the hot broth a ladle at a time, stirring frequently and adding another when the previous is mostly absorbed. Begin tasting around 18–22 minutes; keep cooking until the center is tender with a slight bite. Use only as much broth as needed; if it runs out while rice remains firm, continue with a little hot water. Leave room for finishing additions.
7. **Finish the rice:** Use lemon, heavy cream, freshly grated Parmesan, salt, and black pepper for this stage. Stir in the full heavy cream and Parmesan, all the lemon zest, and the lemon juice to taste. Use the listed salt and pepper allowances. Loosen stiff rice with a little remaining hot broth or water as needed; keep any unused lemon juice in a clean container separately rather than assuming every lemon produces the same amount.
8. **Return the shrimp:** Use fresh basil leaves for this stage. Fold in all the cooked shrimp and basil; warm briefly, starting around 1 minute and checking that the shrimp are warm throughout. Do not extend the rice simmer with shrimp already in it.
9. **Serve:** Use fresh basil (if using) for this stage. Use the optional extra basil, divide among the listed portions and serve immediately. Rice that needs more liquid/time or extra shrimp batches extends the approximate 50-minute schedule.
